sections.html:
Middletown is a township in northern Monmouth County and the county's largest municipality by population, at 67,106 in the 2020 count. Much of its 40.95 square miles of land runs along Sandy Hook Bay, Raritan Bay and the Navesink River, so a good share of houses sit near the shoreline or on creek lots. Before you set a price on a waterfront block, ask a local agent how flood exposure and insurance bills are shaping offers.

The township spans eleven ZIP codes, with postal names that include Middletown, Belford, Lincroft, Locust, Navesink, Port Monmouth and Leonardo. A mailing address with one of those names can still sit inside the Township of Middletown for tax purposes, so check the block and lot rather than the postal town.

Owners live in about 86% of occupied homes here, so the typical seller is a family leaving its main residence, often with a mortgage to pay off on top of any tax balance.

Two offices share the work, both inside the Finance Department at 1 Kings Highway, Middletown, NJ 07748. Value questions belong with the Tax Assessor, while the collector only bills and takes payment.

  • Tax Collection: 732-615-2086. Payment hours run 8:00 AM to 3:45 PM and office hours are 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Monday to Friday.
  • Tax Assessor: handles value, ownership and address changes, and senior and veteran relief paperwork. The township's assessment page links to the Monmouth County record search for assessed values, sales and property record cards.
  • Sewerage Authority: 732-495-1010 for delinquent sewer charges, which are billed separately from the tax bill.

The bill combines municipal, library, school, open space and county taxes. Because those levies come from different bodies, the Middletown collector cannot explain a school or county budget line and will direct you to the taxing authority.

sections.h2: Due dates and the grace period
sections.html:
Middletown's installments land on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. A 10-day grace period normally follows, and if day ten is a weekend or holiday the cutoff slides to the next business day. Pay by 3:45 PM on the last grace day to avoid interest.

A postmark earns you nothing, since the state refuses them, so the money has to be in the office on time. Interest on late payments follows N.J.S.A. 54:4-66. Under N.J.S.A. 54:4-64 a bill that never arrives does not erase the tax, which makes it your job to ask the collector what is due.

You receive one annual bill. The first-half payment is a preliminary half of last year's taxes, and the second-half bill takes that estimate off the final total once the rate is set. At closing, pass the bill to the buyer or the buyer's paying agent. Extra copies cost a fee.

sections.h2: How the Middletown tax sale works
sections.html:
State law requires a yearly tax sale, and Middletown conducts an accelerated electronic one. The township set December 17, 2026 as its 2026 sale date. Once a parcel is close to the sale, payments have to be guaranteed funds such as an attorney trust check, title company check, cashier's check or money order, and card or ACH payments are no longer taken.

An unpaid parcel picks up added costs once it enters the sale process:

  • A 2% cost of sale, with a $15 minimum and a $100 maximum.
  • A $25 mailing fee for each of two scheduled mailings.
  • Delinquent taxes plus interest, added to those fees for the total due.

The township will not waive these fees, and a lost notice does not undo the sale. Holding a lien never entitles its buyer to occupy the house, since possession comes only by foreclosure. If you have fallen behind, get an exact payoff from the collector and pass it to the title company without delay. Cash payments must be exact, because excess cash goes to the next quarter and no change is returned.

The aggregate preliminary net value of Middletown for tax year 2026 was 7.94% above 2025. Higher total value does not mean every bill rises by that percentage, because the rate falls as total value climbs. An owner whose assessment grew less than 7.94% takes on a smaller share of the municipal levy, and one whose assessment grew more takes on a larger share.

Monmouth County uses an alternate calendar, so the appeal deadline is January 15, or April 1 if the assessment exceeds $1 million. The statewide April 1 date does not govern ordinary houses here. Petitions can be filed through secure.njappealonline.com.

Before filing, compare your value with closed sales on the township's interactive sales map, which leaves out distressed sales. Only the assessment can be appealed, not the tax, and evidence should be dated before the October 1 assessment date.

The township's Landmarks Commission reviews work on structures inside the five historic districts: Chapel Hill, Locust, Monmouth Hills, Navesink and Middletown Village. Owners planning additions or changes need a Certificate of Appropriateness. A buyer of a house in one of those districts should know that exterior plans may go through that review.

Houses outside those districts follow ordinary township permit rules. If you are unsure which applies, ask the township with the block and lot number from your tax bill.

sections.h2: Selling a Middletown house with taxes owed
sections.html:
A balance owed here will not stop you from selling. The collector supplies a payoff figure, and your closing agent pays it from what the buyer hands over. Here is a workable sequence:

  • Phone the collector at 732-615-2086 for the balance, quarter by quarter.
  • Find out if the parcel has entered the tax sale process, because extra costs and guaranteed funds are then required.
  • Check any sewer balance with the Sewerage Authority, which keeps its own account.
  • Get the written figures to the title company and your attorney well before closing.

A cash buyer can shorten the timeline, but the payoff, any lien and the recording steps remain. Because bills go out once a year and the second-half amount is not known until the rate is set, ask the collector what has been billed so far and what is still to come, so the title company can split the year fairly between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay Middletown property tax without interest?
faqs.a: It is the last day of a 10-day grace period after each due date of February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, by 3:45 PM. A weekend or holiday on the tenth pushes the deadline to the following business day.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Middletown house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the Middletown tax collector for a payoff figure, and your closing agent settles it out of the sale money. If the parcel has entered the tax sale process, added costs apply and guaranteed funds are required.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Middletown assessment?
faqs.a: January 15, or April 1 when the assessment is over $1 million. Monmouth County follows an alternate calendar, and filing can be done through secure.njappealonline.com.

faqs.q: Who do I contact if my Middletown sewer bill is overdue?
faqs.a: Call the Township of Middletown Sewerage Authority at 732-495-1010. Delinquent sewer charges are separate from the property tax bill.

faqs.q: Does a postmark count for a Middletown tax payment?
faqs.a: No. New Jersey does not accept postmarks, so the payment must be received in the office by 3:45 PM on or before the last day of the grace period.
